stories.original:
**FCA launches AI observatory to track adoption across financial services**

*The platform aggregates real-world examples of AI use by regulated firms, offering the UK's first structured view of how the technology is being deployed in practice.*

The UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has launched what it describes as a world-first platform cataloguing how financial services firms are using artificial intelligence. The resource draws together case studies and data on AI adoption patterns across the sector, intended to help firms benchmark their own use against emerging market practice.

The observatory sits alongside the FCA's broader regulatory programme on AI, which has already included a review scoping AI's implications for open finance and agentic payments, published in July, and the regulator's decision in July to select Anthropic for the second phase of its AI sandbox. The new platform shifts the emphasis from experimental oversight to systematic market intelligence.

The resource offers an early signal of what the FCA considers normal versus novel in AI deployment. That distinction will shape how the regulator approaches supervision as AI-driven decisioning becomes embedded in areas from fraud detection to credit underwriting.

stories.original:
**Singapore proposes first regulatory protocol for verifying AI agents in payments**

*The "know your agent" framework could set a template for European regulators grappling with how to authenticate AI-initiated transactions across open banking and instant payment rails.*

Chia Der Jiun, managing director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), announced on November 19 that the regulator will develop a common "know your agent" protocol enabling banks and payment providers to verify an AI agent's identity, the customer it represents, the authority it has been granted and the limits of its mandate. The protocol builds on MAS's Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime framework, published in July and developed with Ant International, Circle, HSBC, JPMorgan, Mastercard and Visa among others.

Chia warned that some users are already handing AI agents their bank login credentials, leaving financial institutions unable to determine whether the agent is authorised or whether a given transaction falls within its mandate. The protocol is intended to give institutions a structured basis for deciding which agent-initiated instructions to accept, reject or escalate for human review. MAS is also establishing an agentic money sandbox with the Future of Finance Institute to test AI agents using tokenised deposits and stablecoins in corporate treasury and payment scenarios.

The announcement arrives as European regulators work through similar questions. The UK's Financial Conduct Authority published its own agentic finance framework in October, while Visa has expanded its Agentic Ready programme to more than 85 European acceptance participants. MAS's protocol, if adopted, would give the industry its first standardised verification layer for agent-initiated transactions, a problem no jurisdiction has yet solved at the protocol level.

stories.original:
**Devengo raises €5m to scale instant payments infrastructure across Europe**

*A €5 million round adds Mutua Madrilena as a shareholder alongside new funding, as the firm builds on its certification as the first company authorised for cross-border instant payouts.*

Devengo has closed a €5 million funding round, bringing in Mutua Madrilena as a new shareholder as the company accelerates its expansion of instant payments account infrastructure beyond Spain. The raise follows the company's certification as the first firm authorised for cross-border instant payouts under the Single Euro Payments Area framework.

The investment arrives as Europe's instant payments regulation forces banks and payment providers to overhaul their infrastructure for mandatory 10-second euro transfers. Devengo's positioning as a specialist in instant payment account rails gives it a narrow but significant role in a market where many incumbents are still struggling with the operational demands of the regulation.

Mutua Madrilena's entry as a shareholder, rather than a purely financial investor, suggests the insurer sees value in the underlying infrastructure for its own payment flows. The round is modest in absolute terms, but for a company operating at the infrastructure layer of instant payments, the strategic backing may matter more than the quantum.

stories.original:
**Alipay+ connects global e-wallets to Brazil's Pix instant payments network**

*The integration links more than 50 digital wallets to Latin America's largest instant payments system, testing whether wallet-to-domestic-rail interoperability can work at cross-border scale.*

Ant International has connected Alipay+, its cross-border wallet gateway, to Pix, Brazil's national instant payment system. The integration allows users of more than 50 digital wallets and banking apps linked to the Alipay+ network to make payments at Pix-accepting merchants in Brazil.

Connecting foreign digital wallets directly to domestic instant payment rails, rather than routing cross-border retail payments through card networks, is a model that European policymakers and scheme operators are watching closely. The European Payments Initiative (EPI), whose Wero wallet is building its own cross-border capability, faces analogous design questions about interoperability with non-European payment instruments.

Nearly 80 billion transactions were processed by Pix in 2025, making it one of the world's most heavily used instant payment systems. For Ant International, the connection extends the commercial reach of its wallet network into a market where digital payments adoption is already high. For European observers, the question is whether similar integrations between wallet platforms and domestic instant payment schemes will emerge as the cross-border retail payments model matures.
